commitments.text: Route development could negatively impact grizzly bears and grizzly bear habitat. Preserve the integrity of the Iknouk River estuary and riparian areas. Options might include: 1) locating the alignment whereby the route approaches and leaves the estuary at an elevation of approximately 60 m, crossing the Iknouk River on a high-elevation bridge approximately 1 km upriver from the mouth; or 2) locating the alignment up the east side and down the west side of the Iknouk Valley such that the route approaches and leaves the estuary at an elevation of approximately 60 metres (approximately 4.5 km upriver from the estuary). An elevation of 60 m would be sufficient to conserve the habitat values for grizzly bears as well as avoid the possibility of disrupting any mountain goat kidding areas.

Route development could negatively impact mountain goats and their kidding habitat. If such areas are found to exist, alter the route (preferably to an elevation below the kidding area) and/or season of construction accordingly, to minimize disruption of kidding areas and disturbances during the kidding season (mid May to late June).

Route development could negatively impact mountain goat winter range. If such areas are located, and occur within relatively confined areas, the route should be located around (preferably to a lower elevation) such areas.
Route development could negatively impact Bald Eagle nesting habitat. Alter the route accordingly to minimize destruction of nesting habitat.
Prepare a Bald Eagle management plan to address, for example, the timing of construction activities and the impacts of construction on nesting habitat, for all nesting sites near the chosen route.

Route development could negatively impact riparian areas and, consequently, the wildlife that use this important habitat type. Minimize the disturbances to riparian habitats and others adjacent to the Nass River and Iknouk River, and at the mouth of Keaszoah Creek by routing the alignment around, or away from, these habitats wherever possible. This approach is designed to maintain the foraging, resting, and nesting values of this habitat type as well as its value as a movement corridor parallel with the Nass River for several large species of mammals.

Route development will disrupt and reduce the size of stands of old-growth trees that are important wildlife habitats. Some 'Red-Listed' species will likely be affected. Where possible at the eastern end (near Greenville), a route that travels through habitats that have been recently disturbed (e.g., logged, yet away from riparian habitats) is preferable to one through previously undisturbed sites. At other locations along the corridor (e.g., between a point west of the Iknouk River and Kincolith), locating the alignment within the powerline right-of-way will also reduce the amount of old-growth forest that is negatively affected.
